text:
Vancouver arrives on a high and a long slide at once. The Canucks came back from three goals down to beat Anaheim 6-5 in overtime on Tuesday, snapping a ten-game winless run, but they are still 1-4-0 in their last five and have been outscored 24-15. San Jose has dropped two straight, the latest a 2-0 loss to Buffalo, and is playing without Alexander Wennberg and Igor Chernyshov. Collin Graf has taken over a spot beside Marchment and Toffoli, and Ivar Stenberg is up to 18:43 a night. The Sharks sit fourth in the Pacific, six points ahead of eighth-place Vancouver.

Neither side wins the chance battle often. At five on five, VAN has taken 39% of the expected goals (a measure of shot quality) and SJS 44%. Our model projects 3.39 goals for San Jose and 3.04 for Vancouver. The goalies are projected as Leevi Meriläinen for VAN and Yaroslav Askarov for SJS. Askarov has saved 6.7 goals above expected this season (Meriläinen is at +1.4), though both finished well in the red last year.

Macklin Celebrini is our top forward pick at 48% to score and 86% for a point, with 10 points in four games against Vancouver. Elias Pettersson, a five-game point streak behind him, is 67% for a point. Our under-the-radar picks: Karlsson for Vancouver, whose recent shots have been dangerous, and Stenberg, who we have at 59% for a point.
